basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 24.' and it opens 'Vers. 24. Evigilans autem Noe ex vino, cum didicisset. Prophetico videlicet spiritu. Quae'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 24. Evigilans autem Noe ex vino, cum didicisset. Prophetico videlicet spiritu. Quae fecerat ei filius suus minor, ait: Maledictus Chanaan. Notandum | quod, non ipsum Cham, sed Chanaan filium ejus maledicit, qui motus eorum interpretatur, a quo postea dicti sunt Chananaei, quos Dominus ante faciem filiorum Israel ejecit. Quod ergo Chanaan maledicitur, prophetia erat: quia gens illa de loco suae habitationis pellenda erat.
